This '''individual''' worked as a customs official on [[Tregillis]]. He inspected incoming [[Freighter/Legends|cargo ships]] for contraband while simultaneously sizing up likely targets for theft. After the ship was broken into, the customs official by day turned the [[dealmaker]] by night. As a private citizen with «connections», he offered the victims to put them in touch with someone who could provide them with «replacements» in a hurry. He was eventually exposed when he attempted to loot a cargo ship belonging to [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]].

==History==
[[File:Cybot_Galactica.svg|right|thumb|150px|A Tregillis customs official was removed from his position after he tried to loot a cargo ship belonging to Cybot Galactica]]
At some point before the end of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], this person served as a customs official on [[Tregillis]],<ref name="GG11" /> which was situated in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Tregillis system/Legends|Tregillis system]]</ref> He was responsible for routinely inspecting incoming [[Freighter/Legends|cargo ships]] for contraband, charging his own «value tax» on the side while sizing up likely targets for theft. After identifying a likely target, he would sell its manifest information to «the right people» for a profit. After the ship was broken into, the customs official by day became a [[dealmaker]] by night. Acting as the conduit through which the stolen goods were funneled, he made a second round of illegal profit. Later, as a private citizen with «connections», he would approach the party whose ship had been looted and, for a small price, offer to put them in touch with someone who could get them «replacements» in a hurry.<ref name="GG11" />

All went well until the official made the mistake of targeting a cargo ship belonging to [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]],<ref name="GG11" /> one of the [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|two]] largest [[Droid/Legends|droid]] manufacturers and a major force in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Galactic economy|economy]].<ref name="CE">{{CSWECite|I|157|Cybot Galactica}}</ref> The ship's [[Captain/Legends|captain]] contacted his superior, who had his own contacts in the underworld. After some negotiation, it was decided that the official had shown exceptionally poor judgment and should be retired from his position. Three [[Standard day/Legends|days]] later, the disgraced dealmaker was permanently removed from his position as a customs official.<ref name="GG11" />

==Behind the scenes==
This person was first mentioned in the [[1994]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 11: Criminal Organizations]]'', published by [[West End Games]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The short story about a Tregillis customs official was presented in the «Gamemaster Note» section under the description of the dealmaker profession.<ref name="GG11" />
